comparator.name: Bachelor Chemical Engineering and Chemistry
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 Chemical Engineering and Chemistry after-revision OER and appendices were freshly retrieved and inspected on 8 October 2026. All 27 required-course/project/open-space positions total 180: core 125 including 6BFR01 Bachelor Final Project 15, ITEC 10, free 45. Year one is core 60; year two core 35 + ITEC 5 + electives 20; year three taught core 15 + project 15 + ITEC 5 + electives 25. Current 6BBR03 Calculus for Chemical Engineering and Chemistry replaces older 2WCB0. Required 6CBL02 is CBL Process Technology; optional Process Dynamics and Control 6BER07, Analytical Chemistry 8BE150 and CBL Process Design 6BER11 are not universally compulsory and are not added. The current ordinary programme is English; announced 2027–2028 Dutch/English tracks do not alter current instruction metadata. PPD is embedded, MyFuture carries no extra EC and five Studium Generale activities belong within ITEC obligations. Free electives require at least 30 EC at levels 2/3 including 15 at level 3, approval and non-overlap. The ordinary three-year BEP is scheduled in quarter 4 as a block; students enrolled longer than three years may use other quarters. BEP entry requires at least 120 credits including all compulsory first-year components and at least 40 EC of post-propaedeutic core, including 6CBL01 CBL Molecules and Materials or 6CBL02 CBL Process Technology. Admission to 6CBL02 requires Physical Transport Phenomena 1 (6BPR01) and Chemical Reactors (6BPR04) each completed with at least 6, or an alternative partial-test route specified in Appendix 2; the representative curriculum includes both foundations. The interdisciplinary challenge requires prior completion of the offered units containing PPD skills. Future course admission and timetabling remain conditions; no new UCR judgment is made.

alternatives.concept: Combine biomolecular and laboratory science with environmental biogeochemistry, materials and resource recovery, lifecycle analysis, renewable systems, mathematics, programming and data methods. This is a related interdisciplinary response to evidenced biochemical and sustainable-chemistry interests, not Chemical Engineering and Chemistry equivalence.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes molecular cell biology, biochemistry, laboratory work and molecular pathology. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and every dependent advanced environmental/resource course. Mathematical Methods precedes numerical methods and probability. Introductory foundations precede the applied research and product-design work.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the academic and mechanical gates. It owns the integrated biochemical, sustainable-material, environmental-chemistry, resource and experimental interests through actual course content. A second specialist chemistry/process route cannot supply general, organic, inorganic, analytical or physical chemistry sequences; chemical thermodynamics and kinetics; polymer chemistry; molecular synthesis; catalysis; transport phenomena; reactors; separations; process control or process safety. The isolated biochemistry, environmental biogeochemistry and sustainability courses cannot be relabelled as that disciplinary formation, so no padded second programme is produced.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce molecular foundations; UCR centres biomolecules, cells and DNA, while the external component also establishes chemical-process engineering.
Both directly study biochemistry and biotechnology; UCR focuses on biomolecules and metabolism and does not reproduce the external engineering context.
Both establish programming for quantitative scientific work; the external component also contains a dedicated linear-algebra strand.
Both establish calculus for later quantitative work; UCR also teaches matrices and differential equations but is not specialised chemical-engineering mathematics.
Both use team design and development around products and materials; UCR teaches general consumer-product development rather than molecular synthesis or materials chemistry.
UCR has no introductory inorganic-chemistry and synthesis laboratory sequence.
UCR has no general chemical thermodynamics and bonding course.
Mathematical Methods supplies foundations but does not reproduce the external advanced chemical-engineering calculus component.
UCR has no organic chemistry sequence.
UCR has no transport-phenomena course.
Environmental Biogeochemistry does not replace a physical-chemistry course.
UCR has no second organic chemistry course.
Sustainability materials content does not replace dedicated materials science.
UCR has no polymer chemistry and technology course.
UCR has no second transport-phenomena course.
UCR has no separation-technology course.
UCR has no dedicated kinetics and electrochemistry course.
UCR has no chemical-reactor engineering course.
No scheduled UCR course reproduces this multidisciplinary chemical-engineering challenge.
The external engineering-ethics unit remains visible; no general UCR sustainability course is asserted as its exact counterpart.
The genuine 20-EC free-elective space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.
UCR has no dedicated chemical-bonding and spectroscopy course.
UCR sustainability projects do not reproduce the chemical process-technology design challenge.
UCR has no advanced materials-science sequence.
The compulsory 15-EC Chemical Engineering and Chemistry final project is not a scheduled UCR course; optional UCR independent research is comparison-only.
The external technology-and-society unit remains visible; no broad UCR course is treated as equivalent.
The genuine 25-EC free-elective space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.

notes.text: The UCR programme combines biochemistry and molecular laboratory work with environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery, lifecycle analysis, renewable systems and quantitative methods. It does not reproduce the target’s general, organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry; chemical thermodynamics and kinetics; polymers and synthesis; transport phenomena, separations, reactors, process control and safety; specialist laboratories or Chemical Engineering and Chemistry capstone.
